column4: reviewer
The evidence describes MFA requirements but does not demonstrate that MFA is enabled and enforced for production privileged accounts.
Operational records show MFA enrollment for 12 of 12 privileged accounts, with zero unenrolled accounts. Confirm enforcement is also demonstrated.
The policy specifies a 24-hour account disablement deadline but provides no operational records demonstrating compliance.
Operational records confirm that all 8 sampled terminated-user accounts were disabled within 24 hours of their recorded termination times.
The documentation establishes a quarterly access review requirement but does not demonstrate that a review was completed.
A completed and dated privileged-access review is documented with no unresolved items. Verify account coverage and reviewer approval.
The encryption standard defines security requirements but does not provide system-level evidence confirming encryption is enabled for sensitive production data.
Configuration records show encryption enabled for all listed production data stores, with no documented exceptions.
The security standard specifies TLS requirements but does not demonstrate actual endpoint configuration or connection behavior.
Endpoint test results demonstrate that connections using TLS versions below 1.2 are rejected and permitted versions are accepted.
The backup policy defines operational requirements but does not provide successful backup logs or completed restore test results.

The documented restore test occurred in Q3 2026. Under a current-calendar-quarter requirement, this does not establish compliance for Q4. Reevaluate against the revised rolling three-month requirement.
The SLA establishes a 30-day remediation deadline but provides no vulnerability tracking records demonstrating that the deadline was met.
Vulnerability tracking records show identified critical vulnerabilities were resolved within 30 days, with no documented SLA violations.
The logging policy describes retention and monitoring requirements but does not demonstrate active log collection, retention configuration, or alert monitoring.
SIEM records demonstrate 120-day log retention, connected production sources, enabled alerts, and a recent security alert that generated an investigation ticket.
The incident response plan establishes exercise requirements but does not provide records confirming that an exercise was completed.
The documented August 19 incident response exercise includes participants, completion records, and identified improvement actions. Verify the exercise year falls within the required 12-month period.
The access policy establishes third-party administrative security requirements but does not demonstrate that actual vendor access complies with them.
The vendor access record documents owner approval, MFA enablement, defined start and expiration times, and evidence that access expired automatically.
